_what: The consolidated Uber Base inventory. Every named component set this repository has any reading of, with the count each reading gave, and the per-set maximum taken as a FLOOR. It supersedes uber-base-keys.json, uber-base-tiers.json (as a count), uber-base-contracts.json and uber-base-real.json as the authority on how much of Base there is, and leaves each of them standing as the record of what it measured.
_the_crop_chain: Four readings, each of which corrected its predecessor and was cropped in the same way while doing it. 16 hand-drawn sets (a style study) -> 92 sets / 3,211 variants from a TOP-LEVEL PAGE WALK -> 126 sets / 4,280 from an INSTANCE WALK that reached 19,406 of the page's 32,123 instances -> 131 sets / 3,425 from a `?depth=4` node read -> this. Every one of them announced the previous number as wrong. None of them asked whether its own reach was the whole file, and each therefore inherited a smaller version of the same defect.
_how: GET /v1/files/<key>?depth=2 for the page shells, then GET /v1/files/<key>/nodes?ids=<id> once per top-level frame with NO depth limit, each response parsed before the next was requested, reassembled and re-read from disk. 139,442 nodes reconstructed against 139,442 fetched. Every INSTANCE carries componentId, and the VARIANT-typed entries of componentProperties name the set's axes, so the inventory needs no plugin, no library subscription and no Figma UI.
_why_the_one_shot_pull_is_not_used: GET /v1/files/<key> on this file answers HTTP 200, sends no content-length because the response is chunked, and stops mid-string. It returned 102,744,823 B against a true 136,114,759 B, and on a second attempt 62,846,637 B. Neither parsed; curl exited 0 both times. Two such bodies compared with each other show a 38 MB difference between files whose documents are byte-identical. vds-figma now refuses a body that begins a JSON object and does not finish one.

the_depth_4_crop_measured._what: Why uber-base-real.json, the reading this repository currently guards as complete, is a crop. Not an inference: the numbers are taken from the complete export by re-imposing its depth limit.
the_depth_4_crop_measured.and_what_that_predicts: uber-base-real.json recorded a components map of 3,516. A depth-4 read of this page can see 3,512. The reading is not approximately cropped, it is cropped exactly where its depth limit falls, and 208 components sit below it.

totals.accounting_check: 3488 set variants + 232 bare component ids = 3720 = every distinct componentId, each counted once

_this_total_is_a_floor_and_here_is_why: A set's variant grid can exceed what the gallery page instantiates, because siblings that were never placed leave no instance to be counted. The floor is the per-set maximum across four readings, so it is at least as large as any of them and cannot be smaller than the truth. Where a reading is larger than the complete export, that reading reached a set's full grid through its parent set; where the complete export is larger, that reading simply did not see the set. Both happen, which is why no single reading is the authority and the union is.

_what_survives_from_the_earlier_readings.base-axis-reconciliation.json: SOUND, and re-checked here: its rows record axis sets that exist in this inventory.
_what_survives_from_the_earlier_readings.uber-base-tiers.json: the TIER ASSIGNMENT survives as judgement about 92 sets. Its counts do not: it is the 92-set page walk, and 73 named sets are outside it.
_what_survives_from_the_earlier_readings.uber-base-contracts.json: its axis CONTRACTS survive and are the best prose in the vendor set. Its denominator does not.
_what_survives_from_the_earlier_readings.uber-base-real.json: its component KEYS survive and are used here. Its claim to be the full library does not: it read depth=4.
